items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: or you played with Elie Wilhoff?

ctx.x: Was it a star? Um, no, it was, uh, it was a, uh, a good all-round band. That was the, uh, basis of it. And, uh, it was a great band to play with. Um. I remember the first time I, I played with them, uh, I became, uh, 50% better player straight away because, uh, everyone played so well, it was so easy to fit in with them. Um. They, uh, when they started, their star was, uh, just a big star. And then, uh, there was, uh, Jeff Kitchen, a clarinet player. Mm-hm. And after he left, um, Warwick Dyer, the trombone…
Well, uh, was Frank Johnson the first band you played with, or you played with Elie Wilhoff?
Uh, the first recognized band. I, I played, played about with anyone and everyone, uh, wherever I could. Um.
